chain.label: IMC prevailed for the night IFR flight
chain.trigger: Instrument meteorological conditions (IMC) prevailed for the flight, which departed CPS about 1915 on an instrument flight rules (IFR) flight plan.

chain.label: Flight conducted at night in dark lighting conditions
chain.trigger: The accident occurred at night in dark lighting conditions.

chain.label: Turbulence encountered en route
chain.trigger: the presence of turbulence would have made it more difficult to control the airplane with failed instrumentation

chain.label: Primary (left-side) attitude indicator malfunctioned in flight
chain.trigger: we're having some problems uh with primary attitude indicator

chain.label: Pilot became spatially disoriented cross-checking the offset right-side instrument
chain.trigger: The pilot's head movements most likely caused him to experience spatial disorientation.

caused_by.evidence: using the right-side attitude indicator would have resulted in the pilot making frequent, rapid head movements to cross-check that instrument with the other instruments
the presence of turbulence...would likely have exacerbated the pilot's spatial disorientation
the rain conditions in which the pilot was maneuvering would have increased the noise level in the cockpit
an aircraft's attitude can only be determined accurately by observing and interpreting the flight instruments and rejecting the bodily sensations associated with the aircraft's movement

chain.label: Pilot lost control of the airplane in a climbing right turn at 7,700 feet
chain.trigger: the pilot lost control of the airplane at 7,700 feet as he was making a climbing right turn

caused_by.evidence: The disoriented pilot may maneuver the aircraft into a dangerous attitude in an attempt to correct the aircraft's perceived attitude.

chain.label: Airplane struck trees and terrain in a steep, high-speed descent
chain.trigger: the calculated descent rate was about 26,000 fpm, the calculated airspeed was greater than 300 knots, and the airplane was at approximately a 60° nose-down attitude

caused_by.evidence: the airplane began a steep descent

chain.label: Pilot and two passengers killed
chain.trigger: The pilot and two passengers were killed, and the airplane was destroyed.
